clue.text: Crazy house internally a big let-down

indicators.note: internally says the second piece sits within the first

parts.note: bats is slang for mad or crazy

explanation.surface: A mad household turns out to be a huge disappointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy house' reads as a funhouse at a fair; 'internally' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bathos is an anticlimax: a sudden ludicrous drop from the lofty to the trivial, a big let-down in tone.

clue.text: President's instinct at the end — no moral code

indicators.note: at the end places the last piece after the others

parts.note: George Bush, a former US president; the apostrophe-s just joins
the id is the instinctive part of the psyche in Freudian psychology
no as a quantity, zero, looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A complaint that the President's gut feeling has, in the end, no ethics behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: BUSHIDO is the Japanese samurai code of honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Bushido is the code of conduct of the samurai, stressing loyalty and honour, so it is an ethical code.

clue.text: It hardly covers resistance from crowd

indicators.note: from here means taken away from, so one letter leaves the crowd word

parts.note: a throng is a crowd
R is the symbol for electrical resistance in physics

explanation.surface: Something offers little protection against opposition from a mob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It hardly covers' reads like a comment on resistance, but it describes a skimpy garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a minimal piece of underwear or swimwear, so it leaves most of the body bare.

clue.text: No way! Preposterous one won't face up to reality

definitions.text: one won't face up to reality

parts.note: no, as nil, looks like the letter O
ST, street, is a way
rich, as in 'that's rich', means outrageous or preposterous

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a ridiculous idea from a person in denial.
explanation.walkthrough: An ostrich, in idiom, buries its head in the sand to avoid facing facts.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone an ostrich is an idiom for a person who ignores unpleasant truths, after the myth of the bird hiding its head.

clue.text: Fat — pull the whole lot in

indicators.note: in tells us to put the whole-lot word inside the pull word

parts.note: to tow is to pull along
all means the whole lot

explanation.surface: An instruction about fat: haul everything inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'Fat' alone is the definition, not a description of the hauler.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallow is rendered animal fat, used for candles and soap.

clue.text: Sally picked up a drawing pin

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so we want a word that is said the same

parts.note: a drawing pin is a tack, so the phrase gives 'a tack'

explanation.surface: Sally bent down and retrieved a pin from the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a woman's name; here it is a military sortie.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a sudden charge out against an enemy, an offensive move.

clue.text: Following one day in city, in a terrible state

indicators.note: following says the anagram comes after the city part
in says the one-and-day letters go into the city

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
one is the Roman numeral I
THU is short for Thursday

indicators.note: terrible signals that the words in a are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: After a day in town, someone ends up in a dreadful condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a terrible state' reads as one phrase, but 'terrible' turns IN into NI, A follows, and only 'state' defines; 'Following' sets that after the city part.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithuania is a sovereign Baltic country, so it is a state in the national sense.

clue.text: See 17
Violently beating ill-wisher inside — how mad can you get?

indicators.note: inside says the rearranged letters go within the other piece

parts.note: 'hopping mad' is as mad as you can get, so the word before mad is wanted

indicators.note: ill here means badly formed, so the letters of wisher are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks how furious you can be at a person wishing you harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-wisher' looks like one word, but 'ill' is the anagram signal and 'inside' the container one; the question stands for the word before 'mad' in the idiom 'hopping mad'.
explanation.definitionFit: Horsewhipping is flogging someone with a riding whip, a violent beating.

clue.text: Regarding last of houses

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the letters sit inside last of

explanation.surface: A phrase about the final one among some houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' looks like a noun but is the verb: the phrase 'last of' houses the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: 'As to' is a preposition meaning concerning or with respect to.

clue.text: Criticised adopted child's query

parts.note: to take up an idea is to adopt it
a tot is a small child; the apostrophe-s joins
to query is to ask

explanation.surface: A rebuke prompted by a question from a foster child.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone to task is an idiom for rebuking or reprimanding them.

clue.text: Cured ailing animal in India

indicators.note: cured, like something put right or treated, signals these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A sick beast in India has been made well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cured' looks like a vet's success; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The nilgai is a large Indian antelope, also called blue bull.

clue.text: 'Blimey, that's not right!' after drain almost gives way

indicators.note: after places the exclamation behind the drain piece
almost says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to suck is to drain

indicators.note: not says the right letter must be taken out

parts.note: crumbs and blimey are both mild exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in dismay as a drain nearly collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims SUCK to SUC; 'not right' drops R from CRUMBS to leave CUMBS.
explanation.definitionFit: To succumb is to yield or give in, which is to give way.

clue.text: This will show when undressed

parts.note: the phrase to be found works as wordplay: its first word is an anagram signal and its second the fodder, showing the word when

explanation.surface: A cheeky line about what is revealed once clothes come off.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: 'rough' is an anagram signal working on HEWN, which gives WHEN. 'undressed' is not about clothing but stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Undressed stone or timber is left unfinished, roughly shaped and not smoothed.

clue.text: One invited to the pub

parts.note: an invitee at a bar is a visitor, and a drink brought in from outside the usual range is too

explanation.surface: Someone asked along for a drink at the local.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue pictures a person; the answer is a drink, an ale stocked for a limited time.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest beer is a beer offered for a short period, often from a brewery other than the pub's owner.

clue.text: Dark and twisted, first king abdicates

indicators.note: a king who abdicates leaves the throne, so this letter departs

parts.note: kinky means twisted or perverted, as well as tightly curled

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word king, its standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A sinister, perverse tale of the earliest monarch giving up his crown.
explanation.definitionFit: Inky means as black as ink, so very dark.

clue.text: Woman has new uniform

parts.note: Eve, the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: A woman has received a fresh outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniform' looks like clothing; it is the adjective meaning consistent.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniform as an adjective means the same throughout, level or regular.

clue.text: Force loosened Ron's extremely strong grip

parts.note: E is the symbol for electromotive force in physics

indicators.note: loosened signals these letters are shaken free into a new order
extremely takes the extreme letters, first and last, of the next word

explanation.surface: Physical force eased Ron's very firm hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loosened' scrambles RONS with SG (the ends of 'strong') into NGROSS.
explanation.definitionFit: To grip a reader or audience is to hold their full attention, absorb them.

clue.text: Yes, saw a Cambodian for treatment for a very long time

indicators.note: treatment, like processing or working over, says these letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: A man from Cambodia was seen for some medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for treatment' scrambles YES SAW A CAMBODIAN; the phrase means since the beginning of humanity.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means for ages, since the first man walked the earth.

clue.text: School garden party — head not required to take part

parts.note: a comp is a comprehensive school in Britain

indicators.note: head not required says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a fete is an outdoor fundraising party

explanation.surface: A notice that the headteacher need not attend the school's summer fair.
explanation.walkthrough: A comprehensive is a British state secondary school. 'head' looks like the headteacher; it is the first letter of FETE.
explanation.definitionFit: To compete is to participate in a contest, to take part.

clue.text: Grew in volume during a bad-mannered broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means put out on air, so the word is the one heard

parts.note: crude means rude, so the phrase gives 'a crude'

explanation.surface: Something got louder during a rude programme on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grew in volume' looks like loudness; it means amount.
explanation.definitionFit: Accrued means accumulated or built up over time, as interest grows.

clue.text: Country house is good place for shooting

parts.note: a rifle range is a place for shooting

explanation.surface: An estate praised as a fine spot for game shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: A grange is a country mansion with farm buildings.

clue.text: Russia often put this out: 'Support an idiot as leader!'

indicators.note: as leader puts the idiot piece in front of the support

parts.note: an gives the article A
git is British slang for an idiot
a prop is a support

explanation.surface: A political slogan backing a fool for the top job.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitprop is political propaganda, a term from the Soviet Department of Agitation and Propaganda.

clue.text: 'Injecting disinfectant can make everything OK' initially baffled doctor

indicators.note: baffled, as in confused, says those letters are jumbled
initially takes the first letter of each of the words of the quoted claim

explanation.surface: A doctor was perplexed by the claim that injecting disinfectant fixes everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' picks IDCMEO, which 'baffled' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Medico is an informal term for a physician or medical student.

clue.text: Challenged person prosecuting left-winger

parts.note: a DA, district attorney, is an American prosecutor
a red is a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: A prosecutor with leftist views was called into question.
explanation.definitionFit: To have challenged someone to do something is to have dared them.

clue.text: Ruling Tory's name repeatedly disturbing people

parts.note: Michael Gove is a Conservative politician; the apostrophe-s joins

indicators.note: repeatedly says the letter appears twice
disturbing says these letters break into the people word

parts.note: a race is a people

explanation.surface: A Conservative's reputation keeps unsettling the public, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Gove is a British Tory politician. 'disturbing' puts the two Ns at different points in RACE: R-N-A-N-CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Governance is the act of governing, the exercise of rule.

clue.text: Grub up — fish (no starter)

indicators.note: no starter means without its first letter

parts.note: a trout is a fish

explanation.surface: Dinner is served: fish, but skip the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grub up' looks like 'food is ready'; it means dig up.
explanation.definitionFit: To rout is to root about, dig up or rummage, as a pig does in the soil.

clue.text: Very shamefaced about time in order

parts.note: so means very

indicators.note: about says the shamefaced word goes round the time letter

parts.note: red-faced with embarrassment

explanation.surface: Someone deeply embarrassed about timing things properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorted is informal British for organised, dealt with, put straight.

clue.text: Removed undesirables from garden — both of us tricked, some might say

indicators.note: some might say signals a word that sounds alike in certain accents

parts.note: both of us is we, and did is slang for tricked or cheated, giving 'we did'

explanation.surface: Two people cleared the garden of pests, having been conned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some might say' admits the sound is close, not exact, in some accents.
explanation.definitionFit: Weeding pulls out unwanted plants, so 'undesirables' is a fair stand-in for weeds.
